### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **6** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/trigger-record-change`, touching **89** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**16** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 316f7571617e0f22b260c457ec87692f5fc1ff5e`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `organization_id (literal, 41 pages)`
- **5** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **185** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 316f7571617e0f22b260c457ec87692f5fc1ff5e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b71714c59881a459641fb666874c93755167f6ec` — the merge of head `cde16f400e4fc9473fe7786953d0102a1fe8a5e7` into base `316f7571617e0f22b260c457ec87692f5fc1ff5e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b71714c59881a459641fb666874c93755167f6ec && git checkout b71714c59881a459641fb666874c93755167f6ec
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 316f7571617e0f22b260c457ec87692f5fc1ff5e cde16f400e4fc9473fe7786953d0102a1fe8a5e7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 316f7571617e0f22b260c457ec87692f5fc1ff5e && git merge --no-ff cde16f400e4fc9473fe7786953d0102a1fe8a5e7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 316f7571617e0f22b260c457ec87692f5fc1ff5e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 316f7571617e0f22b260c457ec87692f5fc1ff5e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Order of record: the security seat's private order, maintainer ruling "⑤ A" of 2026-11-22. No card. Check-runs on this head: 40 success, 15 expected skip, 0 failed, 0 pending.

### ① Derived judgments

- A read (find, findOne, count, aggregate) by an elevation whose caller the wall denies resolves to zero rows with no error: the deny sentinel is AND-composed onto the predicate, and the count fallback re-enters find. Right (ADR-0123 D2 read rule, ADR-0095 D1 fail-closed).
- Its insert and update, and transfer and restore through the lifecycle mapping, are refused `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, naming the missing active organization, or the missing membership for a person outside every organization. Right (ADR-0123 D2 and D4). The code is the standard catalog's; no new code.
- Its delete and purge are refused the same way. Wrong against ADR-0123 D2's own delete sentence: S1.
- Who is judged: `isSystem` AND (`flowRunId` OR the app-automation mark), carrying a `userId` or the guest envelope. Right as the predicate the two sibling refusals read. Reading a flow run's `userId` as its caller is wrong for one segment: M2.
- Who is not judged: a caller with an active organization (returned before any resolution), an elevation with no caller, and every platform system context (no run, no mark). Right as a served set; the scope of the statement is M1.
- The exemptions are the ladder's own, computed over the caller's context and sets (an object outside tenancy, an object with no organization column, the operator's crossing, the verified owner's read). Right for an action body and a system hook, which carry the caller's envelope whole. For a system flow see M1.
- Permission sets that cannot be resolved become no sets, which grant no exemption. Right; it fails closed.
- The verdict is recorded on a denied read. Right: the engine projects `deny` to the same driver scope recorded or not.
- Public surface: the package index is unchanged; `ElevationSource`, `SUBJECT`, `ELEVATION` and `elevationSource` become module-level exports only. No schema, route or error code moves. Right.
- The two runtime fixtures give their member a membership. Right: under ADR-0093 D8.1 as amended, a person outside every organization reads and writes no tenant-scoped row, so the pins' controls need a member. The pins' subjects are unchanged.
- Evidence: the real-stack pin holds `isolated` for all three kinds and both verbs, with controls. `group` and `single` are held only by module pins over a mocked verdict; see M1.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-security: patch` with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none`, in the PR body and the changeset alike. Right.
- No key, value or type an author can write changes, so the kind is `none`, and `none` ships `patch`.
- The narrowing keeps its BREAKING banner, its FROM/TO and its ADR-0087 disposition (`not-required`, no-migration-prescription), the same disposition the ledger limit's changeset took.
- Only plugin-security publishes; the organizations and runtime paths are tests.
- The level and both declaration lines stand. The banner's own sentences (who is affected, what is not moved) are corrected with M1 and M2.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Flag 1, an elevation with no caller stays unchanged: answered A. The ruling states the rule against the caller's plain door, and a run for no caller has no door. `runtime-identity.ts` on main already says a run that must cross organizations is a user-less one. One segment of such a run is not unchanged: M2.
- Flag 2, delete refused 403: S1, and escalated to the maintainer there.
- Flag 3, a `single`-posture person outside every organization is walled: answered A. ADR-0093 D8.1 as amended (ruling 6796108313) makes a current membership the condition of a person's data access under every posture, and ADR-0123's 2026-11-11 amendment gives that person these same answers under `single`. The caller's door is the rule there too. Scope of enforcement: M1.
- Adjacent item (2): answered in the seat's private note (P1) and carried by M1.
- SQL push-down: no finding. The diff materialises no ids and joins nothing in the application. A denied read is one constant predicate on the statement the driver already runs, and a denied write is refused before any read.

### ④ Design judgment

Against ADR-0095 D1 ("Layer 1's bypass no longer implies Layer 0's") and ADR-0123 D1/D2, the narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real for the caller the wall denies, at the predicate the ruling named, ahead of the bypass. It does so without a second ladder: the verdict is `computeTenantLayer0Verdict` over the caller's context.

Tried to break it:
- Shedding the mark: held. It is a symbol only server code sets. It rides every spread, is carried across the context parse, and is kept by `sudo()` and by the platform-system api on an app-authored or dispatched-action api. A flow's `flowRunId` rides the run envelope.
- A verb the wall misses: none found. A sandboxed body reaches data only through the repository verbs (find, findOne, insert, update, updateById, delete, deleteById, count, aggregate, execute). Each is an engine verb that runs the middleware. There is no bulk, upsert or raw path on that api, and purge and restore are refused by class.
- A client-supplied caller or organization: held. The wall reads `userId`, `principalKind`, `tenantId` and `accessible_org_ids` off the server-built context. The repository sets its own context last, so a query bag cannot replace it. The active organization comes from the session, the key or the guest derivation, vetted against membership.
- Unresolvable permission sets: fails closed.
- Every posture: `isolated` holds for the three kinds. `group` and `single`: M1.
- A declared capability taken away: M2.

M1 (must-fix) — The published statement of the rule (the changeset, register row 1c, the module header) and the rule this diff holds differ in scope in two places, named in the seat's private note (P1, P2). The fix holds the rule in both, or states it as narrowly as it is held. Either way it pins every posture and every elevation kind the statement names on the real stack, with a system flow's pin built from the envelope a run really carries.

M2 (must-fix) — A system flow that started for no caller and then passes a human decision is judged from that point as run for a caller with no active organization. Under a walled posture its reads of tenant-scoped objects resolve to nothing and its writes are refused, with a sentence telling the decider to select an organization. The changeset says system work that runs for no caller is unchanged. The published `runAs` text (`flow.zod.ts` on main) says a system flow keeps system privileges after a decision, the decider being its attribution user. Read in `run-resume.ts` (`deciderSegmentContext`) and `runtime-identity.ts` (`resolveRunDataContext`): the decided segment carries the decider as `userId` and only the run's own organization, of which such a run has none. Derived by reading, not run; reproduce on the real stack first. Fix: decide whose wall binds a decided segment and carry what that wall reads, or leave a run that began with no caller unjudged. Pin the result.

S1 (should-fix) — Dev flag 2. ADR-0123 D2 puts `delete` under the read rule on purpose: it "places nothing and decides no tenant", matches no row, and the boundary is "stated so the next author does not read its absence as an oversight". The diff refuses a denied elevation's delete and purge with 403 and cites D2 for it, in the refusal's developer text, the register row and the changeset. Under Prime Directive 13 the opposite of a recorded decision needs the decision recorded. Either answer delete and purge by the read rule (a predicate delete matches nothing; a by-id delete answers as a row that is not there), or keep 403 on the maintainer's word, recorded as a note on ADR-0123, and cite that. Escalated to the maintainer: does "writes are refused 403" in the ruling include delete? Reviewer's reading: the ruling cites D2, so D2's boundary stands until the note exists.

S2 (should-fix) — The published descriptions that say what elevation does not reach (flow `runAs`, hook `runAs`, action `body` in `packages/spec`) state the two sibling limits and not this one. The ledger limit's change stated its rule there. An author reading "system = elevated (bypasses RLS)" learns nothing of the organization wall. State the rule in those descriptions, with the regenerated artifacts; a description only, so `Metadata-protocol` stays `none`.

N1 (nit) — The swallowed permission-set resolution failure logs nothing, where the plain door logs the same failure. One warn line.

N2 (nit) — The caller's whole layered filter is computed for a Layer 0 question, on a fresh caller context per operation, so the per-request memos (membership staging, the verified-owner probe) do not hold across a denied elevation's operations. Only a caller the wall can deny pays it.

N3 (nit) — The changeset's list of refused verbs omits `transfer`, which the lifecycle mapping refuses with update.

N4 (nit) — For the guest entry's envelope the refusal says "the user" and "join or select an active organization"; a guest has neither.

N5 (nit) — A union-scope member's elevated insert with no active organization, and a crossing operator's, are answered by the engine's organization check, not by D2's 403 that ADR-0123's 2026-10-20 amendment gives the plain door. Nothing lands either way; only the answer differs.
